Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear payload and the call yesterday. Short answer up front: system prompts are counted as input tokens; model-generated content returned to the caller is counted as output tokens; tool outputs are charged as output tokens only if the model emits them in the final assistant response. Rounding is done per-request (per API call) after summing input and output tokens; we round up to the next whole token for each category and then aggregate.

I'll put together a short worked example below. Ben (copied) can confirm behavior for tool integrations and streaming. Let me know if you want a one-line SOW sentence we can lock-in.

Worked example (based on your sample):
- system prompt: 60 tokens (counts as INPUT)
- user message(s): 280 tokens (INPUT)
- model generates: 95.3 tokens (OUTPUT — model text)
- tool call (invoked by model): returns payload ~140 tokens; model includes tool content verbatim in final assistant message (so the assistant emits those tokens) -> those 140 tokens are treated as OUTPUT.

Per-request math:
- total input tokens = 60 + 280 = 340 -> round up -> 340
- total output tokens = 95.3 + 140 = 235.3 -> round up per-request -> 236
- billed tokens this request = input 340 + output 236 = 576 tokens

Important nuances:
- If a tool returns data that the model does NOT include in the assistant response (e.g., used only for internal decisioning), that tool-return is NOT billed as output. The only counts that flow into billing are tokens that traverse the model interface as input or that the model emits back in responses.
- Streaming: tokens streamed to the client are counted when emitted; we don't double-charge for stream chunking, just the final token count as produced by the model.

I'll attach a short summary PDF for procurement-friendly wording.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Hi Olivia — adding some SE-level detail to make sure the SOW examples are technical enough for your budget team. A few clarifying points and one small edge case with tool attachments: 

1) Token attribution details (practical):
   - System prompt text (including any instruction tokens) is always input. If you pin a system prompt at account level in the SDK, those tokens are applied per-request unless you use server-side caching.
   - If you call a tool via the model's tool API and the assistant composes a message that includes the tool output, those tokens are counted as OUTPUT (they are produced by the assistant).
   - If the tool output is only stored as part of session state and never emitted in the assistant message, it is not billed as output.

2) Rounding specifics:
   - We compute raw token counts with high precision internally (fractions). For billing, we round up per-request per-category (input and output separately) to the next whole token. Example: 95.3 -> 96.
   - We do NOT round per-chunk during streaming; streaming only affects visibility. The final billable output token total is the sum of produced tokens after the request completes and then rounded up.

3) Small-call micro-impact example (why procurement worried):
   - Mobile heartbeat call example: system 20 + user 4 (very short) + model generates 3.2 tokens -> input 24 -> output 3.2 -> round up output to 4 -> billed = 28 tokens. At scale (10M calls/month) rounding can move nominal cost by a measurable amount; we can provide a modeled estimate for your expected volume.

4) Attachment/tool binary stubs: if a tool returns a base64 blob that is not emitted in messages, it is not charged as tokens. If you pass that blob into the model as text (e.g., base64 in prompt), it is charged as input tokens.

If helpful, I can produce a short table of scenario -> billed token outcome for your finance team. Also confirming: per earlier, streaming doesn't multiply-charge; we only bill final produced tokens (rounded).

—Ben
